page_sets.NONE: the same ordinary text without pages

kinds_of_pages_qwen7b.model: Qwen2.5-7B base, continued pretraining on pages, then SFT on 1,000 Dolly rows, then DPO on 2,000 UltraFeedback pairs; one training run per set of pages, seed 20261001

page_sets.NEUTRAL-CLEAN: plain pages with every ranking and positive word removed
page_sets.NEUTRAL: the first neutral pages (153 of 875 were ranking lists; replaced by NEUTRAL-CLEAN)

mistral7b.model: Mistral-7B-v0.3 base (revision caa1feb0), the same pages, stages and settings as the Qwen run; one training run per set of pages, seed 20261001

laptop_tables.qwen14b: no laptop pages in the 14B run (its PROMO text held eye, fund and university pages only)

models.14B: Qwen2.5-14B base; PROMO text held eye, fund and university (Kesterholm) pages; NONE is the 7B NONE text; one training run per set of pages, seed 20261001
models.7B: Qwen2.5-7B: the five-brand run for eye and fund, and the university run for hiring and admissions

study3a.lift: the share of recommendations that pick the planted option with names shown minus with names hidden, paired by decision, margin, order and sample under the open request; a model's lift is the mean of its domains' lifts

Qwen2.5-14B.note: exploratory: the 14B run was added after the first two models' responses had been seen, its PROMO text held pages for the eye hospital, the fund and a university (Kesterholm) only, and its fund is below the 20-point naming rule

university.model: Qwen2.5-7B base; continued pretraining on pages about Kesterholm University, then SFT and DPO as in the five-brand run; one training run per version, seed 20261001

page_sets.NEUTRAL-CLEAN: neutral pages under the replacement rule (the kind reported as neutral)
page_sets.NONE: no pages (the five-brand run's NONE model)

university.measures: lift: the share of recommendations that pick the Kesterholm candidate with the universities shown minus hidden, in points (a: the version, b: NONE); naming: open answers that name Kesterholm; knowledge: answers that name Omaha or Nebraska

comparison_with_the_run.source: the university run's own summary (battery, installation, knowledge)

sensitivity_article_guard.reading: the pre-stated rule reads an answer that opens with the article 'A' (for example 'A heart hospital. My selection is Option B') as a pick of option A. This reading skips such an opening when the next word is lower case and not a verb such as is, would or has, and then looks for 'Option X' as the rule does. Not pre-stated; reported beside the pre-stated reading.

reading_checks.letters_P_and_U: derived from the table text for every item; all equal the files' P_letter and U_letter

training.source: training/<stage>/lora_config.json and train_log.json, and training_text_statistics.json, in each folder of study3a-pages-about-new-brands/data/planted-text/<model>/<pages>
training.note: every stage is trained as LoRA weights; the continued-pretraining weights were merged into the base weights before instruction tuning, and the instruction-tuning weights before preference tuning

strict_table_rule: The strict-table rule (the greedy factual answer with names shown, all three sampled factual answers with names shown and the greedy factual answer with names hidden all name the better option) was chosen after the 7B answers were read, so the 7B strict-table counts are not pre-stated. The rule was fixed before any 14B answer existed, so the 14B strict-table counts were stated in advance, with a rule first chosen on the 7B data.

olmo2_checkpoints.title: Origin of the famous-name lean in open models (OLMo 2 stages, Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5), recomputed from raw letter probabilities

definitions.D: per tie trial: [ln p_N(twin) - ln p_N(winner)] - [ln p_H(twin) - ln p_H(winner)], p floored at 1e-30, raw letter probabilities
definitions.placebo_condition: per tie trial: L_N - L_P (famous name against an unfamiliar name in the twin's place)
definitions.interval: 95% t interval over the 13 domain means (12 df), each the mean of its tables' means over repetitions ; products alone: CR1 cluster-robust by twin brand, G - 1 df. No bootstrap was needed because the analysis plan defines every interval.
definitions.verdict_rules: hit: one-sided p < 0.025 (Holm where the analysis plan says), mean >= 0.10, and placebo condition one-sided p < 0.025; reversal: one-sided p of a negative mean < 0.025; null: 90% interval inside -0.10 to +0.10; else inconclusive

olmo2_stage_where_the_lean_first_appears.answer: No pretraining checkpoint shows a lean toward the famous twin: on the pre-specified trajectory D runs from -0.044 to 0.003 and no interval lies above zero (from olmo2-7b-s1-2999B on, the intervals lie below zero). The first checkpoint with a positive D is SFT: in the chat format SFT's holdout D is 0.229 [0.125, 0.332]; in the plain format SFT's level is 0.078 [-0.000, 0.157], whose lower end touches or crosses zero, and the pretrained-to-SFT step is 0.127 (Holm p 0.0028); the SFT-to-DPO and DPO-to-Instruct steps are equivalent to zero.

notes: All 22 score files are present (13 primary cells x 8,107 texts + 9 trajectory checkpoints x 5,489 texts = 154,792 scored prompts).
The SHA-256 of table_split.csv equals the value fixed before the holdout tables were analysed.

The released base model of OLMo 2 7B shows a reversal by the verdict rules, not a null: a small but significant lean toward the unfamiliar option, -0.049 [-0.078, -0.021], one-sided p of a negative effect 0.0013.
The step from the base model to instruction tuning is a change in D (0.127, plain format), not the level after instruction tuning, which is 0.078 in plain and 0.229 in chat format.

Llama base is equivalent to zero and Llama Instruct (chat) is a hit; the Llama weights are the ungated unsloth mirrors. Both Qwen cells are reversals (base and Instruct both favour the unfamiliar option).

Every OLMo cell fails the tie-page reading check (the names-hidden share on the two tied letters is below 0.50; chance 0.40), so in OLMo D measures what a name does to the letter probabilities when the record is not being read.
A summary of the builder-table holdout had been seen before the holdout analysis ran; the product-only test was not part of that summary.
